idea.value: A design studio's 10-second sizzle that proves its claim instead of explaining it: after one tiny line of type saying it gives shape to things, every following shot is a raw element (a pill, a stroke, a square, a knob) visibly becoming finished interface, then a burst of archival and scientific imagery under a fixed caption places the work in a longer history, and the mark is left alone on black.

audience.value: Founders and product teams choosing a product-design partner, and other designers: the film shows interface pieces (toggle, reaction bar, chat bubble, app icon) with coordinate tags as if in a design tool, never explains a feature, and expects the viewer to read meaning from craft alone.

value.device: Flash pre-roll, then a polarity-strobed tiny claim on black, then a long still hold.
value.description: 0-0.30 s: three full-frame 3-frame flashes (navy, black, white) with nothing on them. 0.37 s: a single short sentence in small white type appears dead centre, about a quarter of the frame wide. The whole frame inverts at F16 and back at F23 with a colour-split smear, then the sentence sits completely still for 0.70 s, flares green for 2 frames and vanishes at 1.63 s, leaving 0.23 s of black. The flashes demand attention, the small type in a black field forces the eye to the centre, and the first question is 'gives shape to what?', answered by every shot after.

value.content: One-sentence claim, small type, centred on black.

value.purpose: Proof by demonstration: raw elements become interface
value.retentionDevice: Each shot is one object changing state in frame centre; a navy ground blink every 0.6-2 s
value.content: Gradient pill collapses to an icon that swells into a lit violet ground with guides; a word turns into a magenta stroke; the stroke's angle becomes a light streak on a square; the square turns halftone and becomes a slider knob with rippling rings; a reaction bar isolates one icon that lands on a message bubble.

value.purpose: Argument: place the work in a lineage
value.retentionDevice: Big outline word, then 3-6-frame footage stutter under one unmoving caption
value.content: One large outline word in dashed circles; then archival portraits, an old computer, a laptop, a hand with a card and medical scans, all tagged with tracking boxes, under a small two-part caption.

value.retentionDevice: Only long hold in the film; backdrop dies, mark stays
value.content: Small app-style mark centred on a lit keyboard macro, slow pull-back, keyboard fades to black, mark blinks, last frame navy.

payoff.value: The mark alone in the centre of a black frame for 2.27 s: everything shown before was made by whoever owns it. The film is the portfolio.

callToAction.value: None in words: no address, handle or verb on screen. The mark is the only sign-off.

whyItWorks: Everything happens at frame centre: the title, the icon, the stroke, the knob, the mark. The eye is parked once at 0.4 s and never has to search, which makes 18 cuts in 10 s readable.
It shows instead of tells: the only sentence is 4 words long and tiny; the claim is proven by objects transforming in front of the viewer (a word draws itself as a stroke in 0.6 s).
Contrast of speeds: 0.6 s states, then 0.13 s footage flicker, then one 2.27 s still hold, so the ending feels like a landing.
One accent device (a 3-frame navy ground blink) recurs ten times in a repeating 5 s figure, which gives a silent file a felt pulse and hides state changes.
Archival and scientific imagery tagged with tracking boxes lends weight and heritage without a single claim being made in words.
